reason: Replace the ineffective V1 authorization lineage with a fresh exact-main authorization for the existing PVEP trusted-runner hardening. PR #204 proved that V1 never became implementation authority because PR #202 declared base b1c2ab865a64821956f7f25cb822db61b320e96e while its actual ordinary merge first parent was dfcf813e10d4bdbe49fa9018ec2334a0654ac8a3. The generic delegated-governance evaluator requires exact first-parent equality. This V2 authorization permits the same bottom-layer repair only: deterministic trusted child environment isolation plus safe digest-only failure diagnostics. It does not authorize policy weakening, workflow changes, dependency changes, retries, timeout relaxation, shell execution, candidate overrides, or a new verification framework.

ossFit.basis: The repair is limited to the already-authorized PVEP base-owned runner and its contract tests, using Node.js core child_process and environment primitives. No replacement verifier, runner framework, signing system, command executor, or dependency is introduced.

v1LineageDisposition.reasonSupersessionIsNotUsed: The V1 authorization is not an effective delegated-governance record, and the existing supersession graph requires an effective target record. V2 therefore uses a distinct authorization path and distinct implementation branch rather than declaring an invalid supersession edge.

requiredGenericCapability.name: deterministicTrustedCommandEnvironmentAndFailureEvidence
requirements: Base-owned command execution must not inherit ambient Node process-control variables such as NODE_OPTIONS or NODE_PATH.

The child environment must be constructed from an explicit minimal cross-platform allowlist required for executable discovery and temporary-directory operation; arbitrary repository, workflow, runner, and secret environment variables must not flow through by default.
Environment key matching must account for Windows case-insensitive environment semantics.
The trusted command set remains the sole authority for executable, argv, expected exit code, generated roots, and artifact declarations.
A failed child command must still produce the existing evidence JSON with verificationStatus VERIFIED_FAIL before the runner exits nonzero.

Failure diagnostics written to stderr must be machine-verifiable and safe: include commandId, expected/observed exit code, signal or spawn error code, and stdout/stderr digests, but never raw child stdout/stderr or environment values.
Workspace Head and dirty-worktree fail-closed checks remain unchanged.
No retry, timeout relaxation, ignored failure, fallback command, shell execution, or candidate-controlled override is permitted.

requiredCausalRed: The first V2 implementation commit changes only tests/verification/pvep-trusted-runner-contract.test.js.

A running trusted runner with hostile ambient NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_PATH, and an arbitrary ambient variable must demonstrate that current child execution inherits those controls or variables before the product repair is added.
A deliberately failing trusted child must demonstrate the absence of safe structured child-failure diagnostics while preserving fail evidence before the product repair is added.
requiredGreen: The same trusted command passes when the parent process contains hostile or invalid NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH because those variables are not inherited by the child.
Arbitrary ambient variables and secret-like variables are absent from the child environment unless explicitly allowlisted as platform-critical.
A deliberate child exit failure remains fail-closed and emits safe structured diagnostics with no raw stdout or stderr.
Existing base-owned runner, exact-Head, workspace cleanliness, trusted command-set ownership, evidence digest, and subject binding tests remain GREEN on Linux and Windows.
